scienceChecks: The molecular ion peak has the highest m/z. Fragment masses are differences from M corresponding to sensible losses (15, 17, 18, 28, 29).
notes: Spectrum: outside PracDraw unless James brings spectra into scope.

name: Gas chromatograph and GC-MS (block diagram)
subject: chemistry
draw: Boxes left to right: carrier gas cylinder, injector (sample in), a long coiled column inside an oven, a detector, and a recorder. For GC-MS the detector is replaced by a mass spectrometer. A trace beside it.
params: detector (flame ionisation | mass spectrometer), show the trace (boolean), label mode
scienceChecks: The carrier gas flows through the injector, then the column, then the detector. The column is inside the oven.
notes: AQA names gas chromatography and GC-MS. The AQA teaching guide on chromatography exists; the block drawing is a textbook convention.

name: Gas chromatogram (retention times)
subject: chemistry
draw: A trace with time along the bottom and detector response up the side: a baseline with peaks at different retention times, each labelled with its time, and an optional comparison with standards. Peak area is proportional to the amount.
params: peaks and retention times, standards (boolean)
scienceChecks: Each substance has a fixed retention time under the same conditions. Peak area, not height, reflects the amount.
notes: Graph: outside PracDraw unless James brings graphs into scope.

name: Column chromatography apparatus
subject: chemistry
draw: A vertical column (a burette symbol) clamped upright, packed with silica gel (powder layer) with a layer of solvent above, a band of the sample at the top, and a separating funnel or dropper above supplying solvent. Below the tap a row of flasks or tubes collecting fractions, the first one with a coloured band. Labels: stationary phase (silica), mobile phase (solvent), sample.
params: bands (1 to 3), solvent level, collecting vessels (1 to 4)
scienceChecks: The solvent level stays above the silica (the column never runs dry). The sample band is at the top. Fractions are collected in order from the bottom outlet. The column is vertical and clamped.
notes: A new template from existing symbols (burette, clampStand, bossClamp, separatingFunnel, conicalFlask). An AQA paper asks how cyclohexene and cyclohexanol are separated by column chromatography on silica with hexane.

name: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene (apparatus)
subject: chemistry
draw: The cracking apparatus layout: a boiling tube lying almost horizontal and clamped, with mineral wool soaked in ethanol at the closed end and aluminium oxide chips in the middle heated strongly, a delivery tube to a trough and an inverted tube collecting the ethene over water. A note to take the delivery tube out of the water before stopping the heating.
params: catalyst (aluminium oxide | concentrated acid variant), collect over water (boolean)
scienceChecks: The ethanol wool is gently heated and the catalyst strongly heated. The delivery tube end is under the inverted full tube. The system is open only through the trough (S13).
notes: Same layout as the GCSE crackingApparatus with different chemicals. From memory: AQA 3.3.5 lists the elimination of water from alcohols.

name: Industrial hydration of ethene to ethanol (flow diagram)
subject: chemistry
draw: Boxes and arrows: ethene and steam mixed, a reactor with a phosphoric acid catalyst on silica at about 300 degrees and 60 to 70 atmospheres, a condenser separating ethanol from unreacted ethene, and a recycle pipe returning the ethene. Conditions as labels.
params: show conditions (boolean), show the recycle pipe (boolean), label mode
scienceChecks: Unreacted ethene is recycled to before the reactor. The product is separated by cooling. The equation is balanced.
notes: From memory; the AQA wording on industrial ethanol was not retrieved.

name: Ozone depletion by chlorine radicals (radical chain)
subject: chemistry
draw: A chain of steps with radical dots: ultraviolet light breaks a C-Cl bond in a chlorofluorocarbon, giving a chlorine radical; Cl plus ozone gives ClO and oxygen; ClO plus O gives chlorine radical and oxygen; the chlorine radical is regenerated. Each step is an equation with dots.
params: show the overall equation (boolean), label mode
scienceChecks: Atoms are conserved. The chlorine radical is regenerated at the end of the cycle. The overall change is ozone turning into oxygen.
notes: From memory; whether the ozone mechanism is examined in 7405 was not confirmed.

name: Making up a standard solution in a volumetric flask (practical 1)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the standardSolution template: a volumetric flask with a filter funnel in its neck, a wash bottle and a beaker beside it, the solution below the graduation mark, and a label on the neck. Add a second picture of the made-up solution with its stopper and the meniscus on the mark.
params: solution level, stopper, labels
scienceChecks: The solution is below the mark while dissolving and on the mark when finished. The funnel stem is in the flask neck. The meniscus is read at the bottom.
notes: Practical 1 of 12 for 7405. Followed by a titration, covered by titrationSetup.

name: Measuring an enthalpy change by calorimetry (practical 2)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the spiritBurnerCalorimetry template for combustion: a metal can of water clamped above a spirit burner with a thermometer in the water. For a solution reaction use the temperatureChange template (polystyrene cup with lid and thermometer in a beaker). Labels: can, water, thermometer, spirit burner, draught shield (optional).
params: burner and can, or cup and solutions, thermometer
scienceChecks: The can is clamped above the flame. The thermometer bulb is in the water and not touching the can. A cup has a lid and stands in a beaker.
notes: Practical 2 of 12. The temperature-time graph with extrapolation is a chart (calorimetryCoolingGraph).

name: How the rate of a reaction changes with temperature (practical 3)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the disappearingCross template with a water bath: the flask on the cross paper, a thermometer in the mixture, and a beaker of warm water for the temperature control. Label the flask, cross, observer and thermometer.
params: water bath (boolean), temperature label
scienceChecks: The thermometer is in the reacting mixture. The cross is under the flask. The water bath temperature is the value investigated.
notes: Practical 3 of 12.

name: Test-tube tests for cations and anions (practical 4)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the testTubeReactions template with the tests in the list: Group 2 cations with sodium hydroxide and with sulfate, ammonium with sodium hydroxide and damp red litmus paper at the tube mouth, halide ions with silver nitrate then ammonia, hydroxide ions, carbonate with acid and limewater, and sulfate with barium chloride. Labels give the reagent and the result.
params: which tests, observations, litmus paper (boolean)
scienceChecks: Each result matches its test: the halide precipitates are white, cream and yellow, the chloride dissolving in dilute ammonia, the bromide in concentrated ammonia and the iodide not at all; ammonium gives ammonia that turns damp red litmus blue; sulfate gives a white precipitate with barium chloride.
notes: Practical 4 of 12. AQA's webinar says the handbook's example for this practical does not contain all the tests, so check the list.

name: Distillation of a product from a reaction (practical 5)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the distillation template: a round-bottomed flask in a heating mantle, still head with a thermometer in an adaptor, a Liebig condenser sloping down with water in at the lower port, a receiver adaptor and a conical flask. Labels for each part and the water direction.
params: heating (mantle | gauze), thermometer position, labels
scienceChecks: The system is open to the air at exactly one point (S13). Cooling water enters at the lower port. The thermometer bulb is level with the side arm. The condenser slopes downward.
notes: Practical 5 of 12; also used in practical 10.

name: Tests for alcohols, aldehydes, alkenes and carboxylic acids (practical 6)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the testTubeReactions template, with a beaker of warm water for the aldehyde tests. Tubes: acidified dichromate with an alcohol or aldehyde (orange to green), Tollens' reagent with an aldehyde (silver mirror), Fehling's or Benedict's solution (brick-red precipitate, the Brick-red preset), bromine water with an alkene (orange to colourless), sodium carbonate with a carboxylic acid (bubbles).
params: test and organic compound, result
scienceChecks: The colour change matches the test. A ketone gives no change with Tollens' or Fehling's. Tollens' and Fehling's tubes sit in a warm water bath.
notes: Practical 6 of 12.

name: Measuring rate by initial rate and by continuous monitoring (practical 7)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the rateGasSyringe template for volume against time, the massLoss template for mass against time, or the disappearingCross template for a clock reaction. A colorimeter route uses the instrument box symbol. Labels as in the GCSE pictures.
params: method (gas syringe | mass loss | clock reaction | colorimeter), reagent labels
scienceChecks: A gas syringe system is closed except for the syringe. A mass-loss flask has a cotton wool plug. The measuring device matches the quantity in the title.
notes: Practical 7 of 12. AQA names the methods, not one apparatus.

name: Measuring the EMF of an electrochemical cell (practical 8)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the electrochemicalCell template: two beakers with metal strips in their own solutions, a salt bridge (filter paper soaked in potassium nitrate) between them, and a high-resistance voltmeter joined to the two strips. Mark the positive and negative terminals and the cell notation.
params: metals and solutions, salt bridge, voltmeter reading
scienceChecks: Each metal dips in its own ion solution. The salt bridge dips into both solutions. The voltmeter is across the two electrodes.
notes: Practical 8 of 12. The standard hydrogen electrode picture is a separate row (standardHydrogenElectrode).

name: pH change in a titration with a pH meter (practical 9)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the phCurve template: a beaker on a hot plate with a stirrer bar, a pH probe in the solution wired to a pH meter, and a burette above. Labels for the probe, meter, burette and stirrer.
params: stirrer on or off, meter reading
scienceChecks: The probe is in the solution and away from the stirrer bar. The burette tip is above the liquid. The meter is joined to the probe.
notes: Practical 9 of 12. The curve itself is a chart (phCurves).

name: Heating under reflux (practical 10)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the reflux template: a round-bottomed flask with anti-bumping granules in a heating mantle, an upright Liebig condenser with water in at the lower port and out at the upper port, a clamp at the flask neck. A label says that the top of the condenser is open to the air and is the only opening.
params: heating (mantle | water bath), labels
scienceChecks: The top of the condenser is the only opening (S13). Water enters at the lower port. The flask is clamped at the neck. Anti-bumping granules are in the liquid.
notes: Practical 10 of 12 (preparing an organic solid or liquid).

name: Separating and drying an organic liquid (practical 10)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the separatingFunnelUse template: the funnel clamped upright with the stopper off, two layers labelled aqueous and organic, a beaker under the tap. For drying, a conical flask with the organic liquid and a spatula of anhydrous drying agent.
params: layers and labels, stopper on or off, drying step (boolean)
scienceChecks: The denser layer is the lower one. The stopper is removed when the tap is opened. The beaker is under the stem.
notes: Practical 10 of 12.

name: Filtration under reduced pressure and recrystallisation (practical 10)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the buchnerFiltration template: a Buchner funnel with filter paper in a one-hole bung on a Buchner flask, the side arm joined by thick rubber tube to a pump (label: to pump), the solid on the paper and the filtrate in the flask.
params: solid on the paper, filtrate level, labels
scienceChecks: The side arm is joined to the pump. The funnel stem passes through the bung into the flask. The filter paper lies flat and covers the holes.
notes: Practical 10 of 12.

name: Measuring a melting point to test purity (practical 10)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the meltingPoint template: a melting point apparatus block with a thermometer and a capillary tube holding the solid, both in the holes of the heated block. Labels for thermometer, capillary tube and sample.
params: sample level, thermometer reading
scienceChecks: The sample is at the bulb level of the thermometer. The capillary tube is sealed at the bottom.
notes: Practical 10 of 12.

name: Test-tube reactions of transition metal ions in solution (practical 11)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the testTubeReactions template with tubes of aqueous ions and their products: copper(II) blue with a pale blue precipitate and a deep blue solution in excess ammonia, iron(II) pale green, iron(III) yellow-brown, chromium(III) green, and vanadium in its four oxidation states reduced with zinc (yellow, blue, green, violet). Labels give the ion and the colour.
params: ion, reagent, colour
scienceChecks: Vanadium colours: VO2+ yellow, VO2+ blue, V3+ green, V2+ violet. The precipitate colours match the ion. Cobalt colours are not required.
notes: Practical 11 of 12. The AQA teaching guide says the cobalt colours are no longer required and the vanadium colours are.

name: Separating species by thin-layer chromatography (practical 12)
subject: chemistry
draw: Use the tlc template: a beaker with a little solvent, a plate leaning in it with the pencil start line above the solvent, a watch glass as a lid, and the developed spots and solvent front. Add the Rf measurement lines as for the GCSE chromatogram.
params: spots, front, developed (boolean), lid on
scienceChecks: The start line is above the solvent level. The plate leans on the beaker wall. The lid covers the beaker. Rf is the spot distance divided by the solvent front distance.
notes: Practical 12 of 12. AQA has no equipment set-up guide for this practical.
